title: The Plants That Saved Every Drop
intro: This quiz follows Riya and Caleb as they discover how desert plants conserve and collect water.

questions.prompt: Why do many desert plants have spines instead of large leaves?
choices: To attract more animals
To reduce water loss and protect the plant
To collect sunlight at night
To make the plant grow taller
questions.explanation: Desert plants have spines instead of large leaves to reduce water loss and protect the plant.

questions.prompt: Where does a cactus store water?
choices: Inside its thick stem
Inside its flowers
Inside its spines
Under its bark
questions.explanation: A cactus stores water inside its thick stem.

questions.prompt: How do aloe and agave leaves help the plants survive?
choices: Their thick, waxy leaves help keep moisture inside
Their leaves fall off every morning
Their leaves absorb food from insects
Their leaves produce rain
questions.explanation: Aloe and agave have thick, waxy leaves that help keep moisture inside.

questions.prompt: How do mesquite trees find water in dry places?
choices: They collect water only from their leaves
They grow deep roots that reach underground water
They store water inside their flowers
They wait for animals to bring water
questions.explanation: Mesquite trees grow deep roots that reach underground water.

questions.prompt: Why do some desert plants have wide, shallow roots?
choices: To quickly absorb rainwater near the surface
To hold their flowers above the ground
To keep insects away
To produce more seeds
questions.explanation: Wide, shallow roots help desert plants quickly absorb rainwater near the surface.
